races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden
O'Driscolls Irish Whiskey Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type for Denis Hogan with a fade warning; only 1 day since last run raises a significant fitness/freshness query, and sim-going form at 7f on Good is limited to 0W2P across 10 runs — hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Variance
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a fade flag and a career record showing no wins or places on similar going; steps back to 7f from 8f+ trips with moderate recent form, and Rory Cleary's yard is in quiet form (T14: 0/2).

runners_data.name: Princess Chloe
runners_data.note: Showed a placing at 6f on Good 14 days ago for a claimer booking; drops to 7f for the first time in a while and holds up naturally — the step up in trip from her sharp recent run could suit if the race develops with late gaps.

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Holds up by nature and arrives 23 days fresh; his sim-going record over 7f shows decent placed efforts, but in this race he is pushed towards midfield rather than his natural rear position — his chance is tempered by racing out of role.

runners_data.name: Baby Basma
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front runner; won at 5f on Good and has run respectably at 6f — the step to 7f is a query, but she has the race to herself up front and Ronan Whelan's positive booking adds confidence to her ability to dictate.

runners_data.name: Will Be King
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type with a fade warning and headgear (tp); his best recent effort was a second at 8f on Soft at Standside, and on Good at 7f his form is sparse — naturally a rear-ranger, here displaced to a midfield berth that does not help.

runners_data.name: Liamo
runners_data.note: Front-to-prominent type for Jimmy Dalton (claimer) who ran twice on Good at Gowran at 7f and 8f this season; headgear (tp) applied, and dropping back from 8f+ trips could sharpen him up as a live pace-tracker in this company.

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse running out of role here; all five recent runs have been over 8f-11f, so the drop to 7f combined with a visor for the first time and a midfield map position rather than his natural rear berth makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: All recent form is at sprint trips (5f-6f) and now steps up to 7f for the first time; Wesley Joyce (3) claims, and the horse's natural style is to hold up at the rear — bumped into midfield on the map, making his chance doubly uncertain on both trip and position grounds.

runners_data.name: Romantic War
runners_data.note: Returned 5 days ago and now reappears; bumper/hold-up pedigree with a fade flag, and his form pattern of 09s on Good and Soft does not inspire at 7f — naturally sits at the rear but is mapped to midfield as the field is full of genuine hold-up types.

runners_data.name: Garryowen Green
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up runner for Andrew McNamara who has recorded 0W0P across five runs on Good, all at 7f-10f; the fade warning is consistent with form, and sitting in a midfield slot rather than her natural rear position only adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Interesting booking in Dylan Browne McMonagle for Paul Flynn, who has been active recently (T14: 4/24); hold-up style with a fade flag, but the form string shows a 3rd and 5th on Good at 7f — one of the stronger hold-up candidates if gaps open.

runners_data.name: Pocket Jacks
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 43 days off for Aidan Oliver with a solid recent record of two placings at 7f and 6f on Good; Ben Coen is an upgrade in quality and his natural position close to the pace suits this race shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Stiorra
runners_data.note: Returning after an extended 296-day absence for Conor O'Dwyer, which is a significant flag; headgear (ht) retained, natural hold-up style but mapped to midfield — the layoff alone makes this a tough reappearance in a competitive 16-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Hero Of The Hour
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent type with visor (v) who has run 6 times on similar going; the form includes a 3rd and 5th at 6f, but steps up to 7f today — a consistent pace-tracker whose experience at this course distance combination has some value here.

runners_data.name: Thumama Sands
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up runner with a fade warning and just three career runs, all resulting in double-digit finishes at 7f on Good; Adam Caffrey takes the ride for a busy Adrian McGuinness yard (T14: 3/32), but the bare form offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Baby Basma is the sole confirmed front runner in a 16-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will be allowed to stride clear from the gates and control tempo at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 7f at Gowran. Pocket Jacks, Liamo, and Hero Of The Hour are the natural prominent types who will sit just off that pace, while a cluster of horses including Roman Harry, Maker's Mark, Stiorra, Garryowen Green, Romantic War, and Mini Cotai are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because this field contains far more off-the-pace types than the visual positions suggest. With Baby Basma dictating an uncontested, measured gallop, the race is unlikely to be truly end-to-end, which will compress the pack behind her and reduce the premium on a late finish. This race shape strongly favours horses racing close to the pace — the prominent trio of Pocket Jacks, Liamo, and Hero Of The Hour are best placed to pounce off a controlled tempo, while the genuine hold-up horses face the additional disadvantage of racing out of their natural role, further dimming their chances of delivering a true late swoop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Baby Basma Controls, Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Baby Basma leads uncontested at a measured clip and the field fails to close the gap in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Baby Basma dictates from the front on Good ground, setting a rhythm that suits her prominently-placed rivals more than the hold-up brigade; Pocket Jacks and Liamo, tracking close throughout, have the best chance of picking her off near the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Baby Basma's gallop is just quick enough to string the field out and the prominent trackers quicken past her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Pocket Jacks and Hero Of The Hour, sitting a length or two off the pace with cover, get a clear run and use their superior form figures at this trip to collar the leader; Liamo also stays within striking range throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If Baby Basma sets a genuinely fast early pace that causes the prominent horses to over-race and crack in the final furlong, leaving a gap for one hold-up runner to weave through.
scenarios.body: Princess Chloe, who showed a placing on Good going at 6f and steps up in trip, or Dawn Flame, who has shown ability at 7f on Good ground for a strong jockey booking in Dylan Browne McMonagle, could benefit from a pace collapse; both face the challenge of getting a clear run through a crowded field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Baby Basma goes too fast for the conditions and fades sharply, causing carnage up front and leaving the race to a late finisher.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Baby Basma's tendency to set a sensible gallop and the fact that nearly all the true hold-up horses are racing out of their natural role in this field; any beneficiary would most likely be Princess Chloe or Dawn Flame finding a gap late.

watchPoints.text: Baby Basma (Ronan Whelan) breaks cleanly — if she is allowed to coast in front unchallenged from the gates, she could prove very difficult to peg back at this trip on Good ground.
Pocket Jocks and Liamo both pressing for the same prominent tracking position early — watch for traffic and shuffling in the first 2f if either overcooks it trying to sit on Baby Basma's quarters.

Dawn Flame has the standout jockey booking in Dylan Browne McMonagle and Paul Flynn's yard is in form (4/24 T14) — monitor market moves before post time as this hold-up runner could be more fancied than bare form suggests.

Stiorra reappears after 296 days off — watch for any significant market support as a sign the Conor O'Dwyer team has her ready, but treat with caution given the layoff and out-of-role midfield position.

The large 16-runner field on a 7f flat track at Gowran creates significant risk of trouble in running for the genuine hold-up horses; any who get blocked or checked on the home turn will have no time to recover.

races.name: O'Driscolls Irish Whiskey Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Eichan San
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with moderate recent form (best effort a 4th on Good) and zero wins or places at this track; Terry Casey claiming 7lb but trainer has 0 from 6 in the past 14 days, making a bold impact hard to see.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: One confirmed front-runner here who maps perfectly to the lead; trainer T G McCourt has one winner from ten recently and the horse is fit (9 days since last run), but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects that in this field the role is surprisingly uncontested rather than natural for the rating.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: True hold-up specialist ridden by Ben Coen who adds significant class; best run recently was a 7th on Good over 8f suggesting the trip drop to 7f may sharpen things, and the 1 win from 15 at similar going demands improvement.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old hold-up type who has placed twice on Good ground and won over 8f at similar conditions; tongue-tie fitted, and a 25-day break after a 5th suggests he returns fresh — his solid placing profile over longer trips makes 7f tight but not impossible.

runners_data.name: The Blue Panther
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose genuine running style is hold-up, pushed up the map only because the field overloads the rear; has won and placed on Good but his STYLE_FIT (0.92) and poor recent record (0049) temper expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: Miqdaad
runners_data.note: Flags a fade-in-finish tendency, and while he has placed once on Good ground the redistribution into midfield disguises a true hold-up nature that may struggle in a moderately-run 7f; 58 days off the track is notable.

runners_data.name: Tariff
runners_data.note: A three-year-old with most of his recent form coming on Standard ground at Dundalk — only one run at Good and that was a finishing sixth; the hold-up style mapped to midfield reflects field crowding rather than natural position, and the fade flag compounds concerns.

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent runner who stays close to the pace and has placed twice in similar Good-ground conditions; trainer Lynch with a recent winner from 3 runners, and a 24-day break from a 4th at 6f suggests this 7f test is within range.

runners_data.name: Leannespour
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old with just three career starts, all finishing badly (15th, 14th, 11th), and a true hold-up style squeezed further back by the crowded field; the fade warning and overall profile make this an unlikely winner.

runners_data.name: Darwin's Angel
runners_data.note: Career best came at 10f-11f on Good, and stepping back to 7f looks a significant stretch for a hold-up type who rarely threatens at this trip; mapped to midfield but naturally wants to come from off the pace, making the shorter distance even more punishing.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with an active profile (11 days since last run), and while naturally a hold-up horse, the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) highlights that midfield is not her home; placed once in six comparable-going runs, and trainer McGuinness has hit three winners from 32 recently suggesting stable activity.

runners_data.name: Incredible Army
runners_data.note: OR=59 makes this a well-regarded runner on official merit, but the fade-in-finish flag and 78-day absence (longest layoff in the field) are genuine concerns; won over 6f on Standard but zero wins or places on Good ground dampens confidence.

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Flags a finishing fade and has been stepping down from longer trips (12f to 7f); showed ability with a 2nd over 10f on Good so the stamina base is there, but getting the 7f tactical shape right from a hold-up position is the key question for Shane Foley.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 6f on Good (1st at Gowran), prominent racer who thrives tracking the pace; trainer Magee has 4 winners from 14 in the past 14 days suggesting a yard in form, and stepping up to 7f from a 6f win is the main query — the extra furlong may suit or stretch.

runners_data.name: Nosmokewithoutfire
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag attached to a horse whose natural style is hold-up, placed in midfield only because the field is stacked at the back; trainer McCourt has one from ten recently, and three runs all resulting in double-figure finishes (10th, 12th, 7th) tell a discouraging story.

runners_data.name: Snap Decision
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a string of 6th, 6th, 8th, 8th finishes and a fade tendency; the redistribution into midfield overstates where this hold-up type will actually race, and the limited form on comparable going (2 from 6 run on Good) offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Dynamic Force is the one confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner 7f handicap, and with no genuine rival to press for the lead, they are likely to dictate a sustainable, controlled gallop from the front on Good ground at Gowran. Glen Breeze and Jackandthefox are the natural prominent types capable of tracking close behind, giving the front end some shape without turning this into a true pace battle. The field is heavily dominated by hold-up horses — The Blue Panther, Nosmokewithoutfire, Tariff, Leannespour, Darwin's Angel, Beau Army, and Snap Decision are all genuine come-from-behind types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because there is no room for all of them to settle where they would naturally want to be; the runners most likely to actually secure prominent berths ahead of the backfield are those with proven gate speed or prominent-running form such as Glen Breeze and Jackandthefox. With one unhurried front-runner setting a steady tempo and a mass of hold-up horses unlikely to get a truly searching pace to aim at, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel in the top half of the field without needing to be covered up — prominently-ridden types with a clean passage into the straight stand to benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dynamic Force Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Dynamic Force is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured, uncontested gallop that suits a prominent run-on.
scenarios.body: Dynamic Force dictates from the front and, with no rival applying pressure, a sustainable tempo means the lead is never seriously threatened until the final furlong, rewarding anything that travels close to the pace; Glen Breeze, with a recent course win over 6f and a prominent style, is ideally placed to pick up the pieces if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Glen Breeze and Jackandthefox push forward and the race becomes a medium-tempo grind won by a horse that travels handily throughout.
scenarios.body: A steady but not slow pace set by Dynamic Force with Glen Breeze and Jackandthefox in close attendance produces a test of straightforward galloping ability rather than a sprint finish; horses who can handle the 7f trip prominently without getting outpaced late — such as Brains, who has placed at this sort of trip — are well suited.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely quick enough — forced by Jackandthefox or Glen Breeze making a move — to string the field and open a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected gallop drains the leaders, and the handful of hold-up horses who manage to find a clear run in the straight can pick them off; Usuario Amigo (Ben Coen in the plate, 7f form, hold-up style) and Sands Castle, who has placed at further and can stay on, represent the best placed to capitalise from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches behind a dawdling Dynamic Force and the race turns into a rough-and-tumble sprint in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With 16 runners and a very steady tempo, traffic problems become acute for the backmarkers and the race devolves into a cavalry charge; horses with any tactical flexibility — Brains (placed twice in similar conditions, handles Good) and Beau Army — may benefit from being closer than their natural position suggests.

watchPoints.text: Dynamic Force's early pace controls the whole race — if they miss the break or are crossed by Jackandthefox or Glen Breeze pushing forward, the assumed lead scenario unravels immediately.
Glen Breeze steps up from 6f to 7f for the first time in a 16-runner field; if the extra furlong proves too much late on, the front-end scenario shifts sharply in favour of closers from midfield.

With at least seven hold-up types all wanting to come from behind and only one true front-runner, traffic congestion in the straight at Gowran is a serious concern — watch for interference blocking runners like Usuario Amigo or Sands Castle from getting a clear run.

Incredible Army and Sands Castle, both carrying the highest OR ratings (59) alongside Dynamic Force, return from the longest breaks in the field (78 days and 12 days respectively) — early signs of rustiness or sharpness from either will be significant for the outcome.

Trainer T G McCourt saddles both Dynamic Force and Nosmokewithoutfire — monitor any market moves between the two as a stablemate tactical ride from the front could be deployed to set up the hold-up runner, though Nosmokewithoutfire's form makes that scenario unlikely to pay off.

races.name: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Amadeus Mozart
runners_data.note: Strong form at 1m4f+ (second twice at this trip), A P O'Brien-Ronan Whelan combination firing well, Good ground suits (4/5 on similar), though STYLE_FIT tag notes he is potentially racing slightly out of natural role as a prominent racer in an unusually pace-heavy field — temper expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Echo Inferno
runners_data.note: Won a 1m5f Listed on Good last time, which is the standout recent performance in the field, but as a genuine front-runner now pushed into a midfield slot by a crowded pace map, she will need to adapt her tactics — Shane Foley's experience may help her find cover and produce a late effort.

runners_data.name: Nil Bua Gan Dua
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners the Joseph O'Brien hold-up specialist who has run seven times on similar going and placed four times; the tongue-tie flag is notable, and from hold-up position on a moderate-tempo card he needs a well-run race to land his run — a small-field controlled gallop is not ideal for his profile.

runners_data.name: Shosholoza
runners_data.note: Runs in the same Joseph O'Brien yard as two rivals but shaped better on Soft than Good (0 wins, 0 places on similar going in five attempts); Declan McDonogh holds the partnership together but declining recent form (6th, 6th, 8th) and a tongue-tie addition suggests connections are searching for answers.

runners_data.name: Believed
runners_data.note: Won a 1m4f Listed on Standard last time and placed at 1m2f on Good — strong credentials at this trip and class level — but as a natural front-runner redistributed into a midfield slot because of the crowded pace map, Ben Coen will need to think tactically rather than simply kicking to the front as Believed naturally prefers.

runners_data.name: Camino Vino
runners_data.note: Returned a distant 13th last time on Good over 1m2f, and 54 days off is notable; the one win came on Standard ground at a shorter trip, and Good turf form at this distance is unproven — raw ability has not yet translated here.

runners_data.name: Saga Gaga
runners_data.note: Two wins from two runs at 1m and 1m2f on Good ground for M D O'Callaghan, rising rapidly in class and distance to Listed level here; the 11-day turnaround is quick, but form is progressive and Good turf suits — a prominent position close to Amadeus Mozart is the natural fit for this style.

runners_data.name: Vauntingly
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f on Good last time and has placed in all four career starts; like Believed and Echo Inferno, a genuinely prominent racer whose natural forward position is unavailable in this field — J M Sheridan will have to settle for cover she is not accustomed to, which is the key tactical question mark against her chance.

races.paceDynamic: Amadeus Mozart is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected, should control the gallop from the outset at a measured, sustainable tempo over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Gowran. Saga Gaga and Shosholoza will push to go with him in the early stages, creating a small prominent group, but the absence of a speed duel means fractions are unlikely to be truly searching. This race shape — a controlled lead, moderate tempo, and a decisive move from the home turn — heavily favours horses who can sit close to the pace or make a forward move two furlongs out rather than those grinding from deep. The field contains more prominent types than the race can accommodate: Believed, Echo Inferno, and Vauntingly are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who will be shuffled back into midfield, meaning their redistribution to that position is situational rather than stylistic, and any reading of hold-up horses mounting a late rally should be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Amadeus Mozart dictates an uncontested moderate gallop and the race is won by a horse travelling in his slipstream.
scenarios.body: Amadeus Mozart sets a manageable tempo, the prominent group conserve energy through the middle stages, and the race is won from close to the pace when the sprint develops inside the final two furlongs on the home straight; a horse who has sat second or third throughout and possesses a finishing kick from that position will be hardest to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Shuffle, Late Power
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough to compress the field and a horse from the rear of the mid-division produces a sustained run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A compressed gallop brings the hold-up horses and the redistributed prominent types back into contention simultaneously, turning the finish into a sprint that can be won by a horse with raw ability arriving late; on Good ground over 1m4f this requires genuine class to arrive in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On, Leader Lasts
scenarios.trigger: If Amadeus Mozart quickens the tempo at the right moment and threads clear before the straight without being caught.
scenarios.body: A strongly run final half-mile from a confident front-runner on Good ground can exhaust the chasing pack if the jockey times the move astutely; Amadeus Mozart's three-year-old profile and Ronan Whelan's positive style make this plausible if less likely given the style-fit discount.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Rhythm, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If traffic issues in the mid-pack or a pace collapse unsettles the fancied horses and creates an opening for a longer-priced runner.
scenarios.body: Camino Vino, returning from 54 days off with solid earlier form, or Vauntingly — genuinely a prominent racer finding herself adrift in midfield — could capitalise if the race falls apart structurally; this scenario requires a combination of errors and luck rather than skill.

watchPoints.text: Echo Inferno's tactical flexibility is the key unknown — if Shane Foley opts to push forward from stall position and contests the pace with Amadeus Mozart rather than accepting a midfield berth, the early order could be sharply disrupted.

Saga Gaga's rapid class and distance rise — from maiden level to Listed over 1m4f on an 11-day turnaround — leaves a genuine stamina and class question unanswered, particularly if Amadeus Mozart raises the tempo in the home straight.

Three Joseph O'Brien runners (Nil Bua Gan Dua, Shosholoza, Vauntingly) create potential for a team strategy; watch for early signals on which horse the yard is riding to win, as a sacrificial lead from Vauntingly is possible if connections want pace injected.

Believed's proven 1m4f Listed form on Good is the most directly relevant recent benchmark in the field, but her comfort zone is setting or tracking the pace — monitor how Ben Coen positions her in the first two furlongs, as a crowded early sequence could compromise her entire race.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Highway Safety Developments Handicap

runners_data.name: Harana
runners_data.note: D.K. Weld's four-year-old has strong course-and-distance profile with a recent placed effort at this trip on Good, rides off OR 80 at the top of the weights, and Chris Hayes's hold on this type of race is a significant positive; a natural prominent mover who simply needs a clean run at the two-furlong pole.

runners_data.name: Frank Pickle
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes over on this five-year-old who put up a game effort to win over this exact course and distance 16 days ago, giving him a form line that is directly relevant; prominent style suits a race with one front-runner, and the Foster yard is in decent recent form with 1 from 3 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Ocean Manifest
runners_data.note: Stephen Thorne's charge is a prominent racer whose best form has come on Standard ground rather than Good, so the going here is a mild step up in conditions; the tongue-tie is worn again and Jack Kearney's 3lb claim reduces the weight burden, but the string of STA victories makes the going switch a small but genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: Jack Foley's three-year-old arrives 27 days between runs having shown earlier promise with a win at 7f and placed effort over 9f on Good, but form since has regressed with three disappointing finishes; DBM's booking is eye-catching and the prominent style is suited, though the current OR trend is heading the wrong way.

runners_data.name: Hambelton
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-horse field, trained by David Marnane who is 2 from 22 in the last 14 days, and arrives with strong recent form including a win and a second over this exact course, distance, and going; his ability to lead without a challenger is the single most important structural factor in this race.

runners_data.name: Snow Princess
runners_data.note: Jack W. Davison's three-year-old has a running style that is currently unclassified and returns after a significant 101-day absence; all three career runs have come on Soft or Standard, making today's Good ground a new surface question, and the yard has had no winners from its last three runners in the fortnight.

runners_data.name: Red Hugh O'Donnell
runners_data.note: Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim softens the burden on this hold-up type whose best form includes a recent win on Soft, and a previous course run of 14th on Good is not encouraging at this venue; the tongue-tie is fitted again and with only 11 days since last run he is fresh, making him the most credible late finisher if the prominent pack ties up.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and runs this four-year-old who carries a tongue-tie and has placed here twice over 8f on Good — genuine course form — but his natural style is front-end prominent, and in a field already crowded at that position he is likely to find himself further back than he'd ideally want, blunting his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's eight-year-old has a solid recent form line including two thirds over this trip on Good, and runs with hood and tongue-tie again; like Zaraahmando he prefers to race up with the pace but will likely be pushed back by the prominent traffic, meaning he will be racing in a role that doesn't fully complement his strengths today.

races.paceDynamic: Hambelton is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious rival prepared to take him on for the lead, he should be allowed to dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop over Gowran's flat mile. Four of the nine runners carry prominent intentions — Harana, Frank Pickle, Ocean Manifest, and Liberation Date — creating a congested pack behind Hambelton from the outset, with real traffic risk emerging two to three furlongs out as those horses jostle for the best position approaching the home turn. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can comfortably absorb: Zaraahmando and No More Porter are genuine prominent racers who will likely find themselves shuffled back into a midfield role against their nature. With Hambelton able to control tempo without being pressured and a cluttered middle section likely generating interference, this race shape most strongly favours a relaxed, close-up prominent runner who can sit second or third on the outside and produce a clean run from two out — rather than a hold-up horse needing daylight through a compressed field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hambelton Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Hambelton sets a fair but unhurried pace and the prominent chasers get clear passage into the straight.
scenarios.body: Hambelton controls fractions from the front, and the horses travelling just behind him on the outside — Harana, Frank Pickle — get first run entering the final two furlongs where the contest is decided on merit over the flat finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hambelton Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo drops low enough that Hambelton's ability to control the race converts into a winning front-running performance.
scenarios.body: Sitting uncontested in front, Hambelton slows the pace to a crawl and times his run to the line perfectly, his rivals finding themselves unable to close as he quickens away in the final furlong; his recent course form over this exact trip and surface underpins this threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Late Swooper
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack becomes hopelessly bunched rounding the home turn and closers find a gap late.
scenarios.body: The four prominent runners create a wall three wide entering the final two furlongs, forcing brief checks and leaving Red Hugh O'Donnell or a recovered Zaraahmando to thread through for a late strike; this scenario is constrained by Zaraahmando's redistribution from his natural prominent role, meaning he is not operating at full tactical efficiency.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes Hambelton to quicken earlier than ideal and the race degenerates into a scramble.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run middle section followed by a sudden sprint suits a fresh or lightly-raced runner catching rivals flat-footed; Snow Princess, returning from 101 days off and with unknown tactical tendencies, represents this wildcard, though the scenario depends on circumstances well outside the likely race shape.

watchPoints.text: Hambelton (Luke McAteer) has a clear lead on paper but must not be allowed to slow the gallop to a walk — if he does, his prominent chasers will be coiled right behind him and a furlong-long sprint will not suit a front-runner.

At the two-furlong marker, the cluster of Harana, Frank Pickle, Ocean Manifest, and Liberation Date are all likely to be racing within a length of each other — watch for tight gaps and horses being checked or switched wide, as this is where the race will be won or lost.

Zaraahmando and No More Porter, both natural prominent racers, will be operating out of their preferred position in a midfield role; if either gets an unexpected gap early and recovers position, they become markedly more dangerous than their mapped profile suggests.

Snow Princess returns from 101 days off with no form on Good ground — monitor her in the parade ring for condition and behaviour; if she looks backward, she is likely a non-factor regardless of scenario.

Red Hugh O'Donnell's earlier 14th-place finish at Gowran on Good is a poor course reference, but his hold-up style means he bypasses the prominent traffic altogether — he is the one horse in the race whose chance improves the more chaos unfolds inside the final quarter-mile.

races.name: Tote Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Burford Beauty
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell; 16 days between runs, and her best going form is limited — seven sim-going runs yielding only one place — making a big finish from the rear unlikely in what shapes up as a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and race-shaper; Denis Hogan runner steps up in trip slightly and sets her own pace uncontested — the STYLE_FIT flag is noted but her controlling role here is structural and not assumed away lightly.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has shown versatility in placement and won over 10f on Heather; R P Burns has no recent 14-day runners suggesting a quiet yard, but this horse's form over 10f+ on Good is the best genuine hold-up angle in the race.

runners_data.name: Georg Zhukov
runners_data.note: Dramatic drop in trip from 18f and 16f chase starts to 9.5f flat; form reading is difficult to trust and sim-going figures are weak (4 from 15), making him a hard horse to place in any scenario with confidence.

runners_data.name: Haughty
runners_data.note: A genuine back-of-the-field operator whose natural style is obscured by redistribution onto the midfield map; V C Ward yard has just one runner in the 14-day window, and a history of minor placing on Good but not winning since a 7f start in recent history.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: Last ran just three days ago — significant freshness concern — and the Denise Foster-trained mare has been consistently mid-to-rear of the field in handicaps; her Good-ground form over 8-10f shows repeated mid-pack finishes without a win.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag and a form string showing nothing better than sixth in recent outings; naturally a hold-up horse now squeezed into midfield, and the slow-run race shape over 9.5f is unlikely to produce the sprint finish he would need.

runners_data.name: Lady Luck
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag is a red flag given this race is expected to be run at a controlled tempo; Rodger Sweeney's four-year-old has consistent mid-field finishes on various surfaces and the STYLE_FIT flag further dampens confidence in her finding her natural rhythm here.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago and carries headgear (tongue-strap and blinkers); Joseph Murray's six-year-old has been placed on Good going before but his form string shows nothing above fifth recently, and the very quick turnaround warrants caution.

runners_data.name: Magna Gee Gee
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good and placed twice in similar conditions — the most relevant recent form in the field for this trip and surface; Patrick Flynn has had one winner from six in the 14-day window, and this horse's ability to race prominently or just off the pace gives her a tactical edge.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on Good and has placed three times in six sim-going runs — a genuine closer whose natural hold-up style is compressed by redistribution; Richard Brabazon runner, and if even a small gap opens in the straight, the 9f winning form is directly applicable here.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a fade flag and a form string of 005060 — nothing in recent form suggests he can win from his natural position even in ideal circumstances; W McCreery has been active with 21 runners in 14 days but this runner's own figures are poor.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag combined with a shocking sim-going record (12 from 15 average finishing position) and recent form of 699000 makes her among the least likely winners in any race shape; Andrew Slattery's four-year-old's STYLE_FIT flag reinforces the pessimism.

runners_data.name: My Vonnie
runners_data.note: All recent runs have been on Standside/All-Weather, giving virtually no usable turf form; M M Rice's five-year-old has been consistently mid-to-rear on the all-weather and the switch to Good turf over 9.5f with a STYLE_FIT flag makes this a speculative entry at best.

races.paceDynamic: Hexagonal is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner handicap over 1m1½f on Good turf at Gowran Park, and with no meaningful challenger for the lead, she is set to dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front. The pace is unlikely to be strong — one leader pressing her own tempo over this trip on Good ground typically produces a falsely-run or steadily-run race, compressing the field and making it hard to make up ground from the rear. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types, but the sheer volume of true closers crammed into the midfield and rear means many will not get a clean run or the pace injection they need to deliver late. This race shape heavily favours the one horse who can control the tempo — Hexagonal — and any horse prominent enough to track her without expending excessive energy, particularly those with course form at this trip; true hold-up horses operating in their natural style face an uphill task against a slow-run lead when they cannot generate the pace differential they depend on. The field holds far more hold-up horses than can all settle into their natural position at the rear — Yquem, Morning Approach, Shahada Ace, Jazz Dreamers, Lady Luck and Master Garvey are among those most likely to be crowded forward or denied their ideal berth, with Deuteronomy and Magna Gee Gee the most capable of adapting if ridden with any flexibility.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hexagonal Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hexagonal bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable gallop that suits a prominent finisher.
scenarios.body: Hexagonal controls every yard at a pace that suits her, and the hold-up-heavy field cannot generate sufficient momentum to reel her in off a slow pace; any horse tracking her in second or third is ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting just off Hexagonal's shoulder throughout picks off the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace is slow enough to keep the field bunched, meaning the horse sitting second or third — saving a length or two on Hexagonal — arrives in the final two furlongs with energy in reserve; Magna Gee Gee's recent win over 12f on Good and Deuteronomy's hold-up-to-prominent versatility make them candidates here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Squeeze Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a seam opens between rivals for a well-positioned closer to thread through.
scenarios.body: A congested midfield with many redistributed hold-up types means traffic could be chaotic, but if one closer finds daylight — Yquem, who won over 9f on Good, or Deuteronomy — they could benefit from a sprint finish; the compressed gallop works against most genuine closers, so only the most adaptable benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Hold-Ups Delivered
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses push forward early and force a genuinely strong gallop, turning this into a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: The crowded hold-up contingent scrambles forward and creates more pace than expected, turning the race into a genuine staying test over the 1m1½f trip; however, since nearly all the back-markers are tagged redistributed or style-fit and are not true hold-up finishers in this shape, the chance of this scenario producing a hold-up winner is low.

watchPoints.text: Hexagonal sets every fraction from the front — if apprentice Reese Holohan (4lb claim) conjures even a modest sectional in the straight, the hold-up-heavy field will find it very difficult to reel her in before the line.

Magna Gee Gee's 12f Good-ground win is the standout trip-and-going match in the field — watch whether Robyn Donaghue-Leahy slots her in second or third early, as that position would be decisive in a slowly-run race.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Yquem, Morning Approach, Shahada Ace, Jazz Dreamers, Lady Luck, Master Garvey) will cause significant early traffic behind Hexagonal — watch for crowding and checking in the first two furlongs as they all compete for the same ground.

Deuteronomy's winning form came over 10f on Heatherbys Good — this 9.5f trip on Gowran Good is marginally shorter than ideal, and Nicola Burns will need to position him more prominently than usual given the compressed pace shape.

Three horses (Duchess Anne, Master Garvey, Morning Approach) ran within the last three days — monitor any market moves or drifts late on, as quick-turnaround runners in a 14-runner handicap on Good ground often attract informed money or drift sharply for condition reasons.

races.name: Tote Race

runners_data.name: Benevento
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose recent form reads poorly (7th last time, 161 days off), and the step back to 1m1½f from 7f-8f trips looks an awkward fit; the likely steady pace under Ask Me Again's control offers little for a closer to run into at Gowran.

runners_data.name: Puppet Master
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but has contested trips up to 17f recently, making this 1m1½f trip a significant step down in distance; 21 days between runs is fine, but Good-ground form (8/10 runs) is underwhelming and a slow tempo will blunt any closing kick.

runners_data.name: Spicy Margarita
runners_data.note: Apprentice Paddy Harnett takes the ride on a 7-day turnaround, and while De Aguiar's yard is in form (2/16 T14), this horse's natural instinct is to race off the pace — with the rear positions already congested, it will likely end up further forward than ideal, compromising its best chance of producing a finish.

runners_data.name: Ask Me Again
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, so will get a clear lead uncontested; just two runs to go on (both away from Gowran) and the horse carries a 3yo allowance, but the tactical advantage of controlling a moderate pace from the front is substantial here.

runners_data.name: Goddess Of War
runners_data.note: An unknown quantity with no form to assess and carrying the going-unknown flag — entirely lightly raced and any running style assessment is speculative; Mrs Harrington's operation commands respect but there is no evidence base on which to build confidence.

runners_data.name: Leopold The First
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer (four seconds from last five runs) who should race prominently and box-seat the favourite; Robbie Colgan is a positive booking and the 43-day absence isn't a major flag given the trainer's low-volume operation, though OR 90 is modest versus the top weights.

runners_data.name: Summer Is Tomorrow
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle's presence on an O'Brien-trained 3yo with four places from five on Good ground is a significant positive; races prominently and the step back from 10f to 1m1½f is well within range — this profile sits ideally for the race shape Ask Me Again creates.

runners_data.name: Hollys Graces
runners_data.note: De Bromhead sends out a horse returning from 93 days off wearing blinkers, and while the hold-up style is genuine, the back of the field will be crowded — the horse will likely race a slot or two forward of its optimal position, and a moderate pace does it few favours.

races.paceDynamic: Ask Me Again is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival looking to force the pace from the outset, is poised to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable gallop over 1m1½f on Good ground at Gowran. Leopold The First and Summer Is Tomorrow will push forward from the prominent ranks, but neither is likely to challenge Ask Me Again for the lead, meaning the pace car sets its own terms throughout. The field holds more hold-up types than can comfortably slot into the rear — Spicy Margarita and Hollys Graces are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield because the true back positions are congested, and both will be racing at least partially out of role. This race shape — an uncontested, moderate-tempo lead set by a single front-runner — strongly favours prominent and tracking horses who can sit within striking distance and pounce in the straight, rather than horses needing a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ask Me Again dictates a steady pace unchallenged and the race is won by a horse tracking within the first four.
scenarios.body: Ask Me Again sets a comfortable tempo and the race resolves as a sprint in the home straight, favouring horses positioned just off the pace who can quicken on Good ground; the lack of genuine pressure means hold-up horses are left with too little to close into.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Ask Me Again's controlled gallop proves too economical and the horse simply stretches clear late without being reeled in.
scenarios.body: With no horse applying pressure and the prominent types failing to quicken sufficiently, Ask Me Again banks enough energy to sustain the effort through the final two furlongs; this scenario rewards the lone pace-setter capitalising on a race run entirely to its strengths.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a horse tracking mid-division produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires the prominent horses to push forward early and raise the tempo beyond what Ask Me Again wants, creating a true test that rewards a closer; Summer Is Tomorrow's recent Good-ground form and Dylan Browne McMonagle's positional judgment are assets here, though the likely moderate gallop makes this shape less probable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is unexpectedly strong throughout and genuine hold-up horses are able to unleash a closing burst from the rear.
scenarios.body: Benevento or Puppet Master would need the race run at an honest clip to give their hold-up style full expression, but both are racing at distances shorter than their recent profiles and face redistribution congestion at the rear; the low probability reflects how rarely this shape materialises when a single uncontested front-runner controls the tempo.

watchPoints.text: Ask Me Again holds the tactical keys to this race — if J M Sheridan gets a clean break and settles into a rhythm on the front end, no other runner is positioned to disrupt the tempo, making the likely race shape a near-certainty.

Summer Is Tomorrow is the most dangerous prominent tracker in the field: watch where Dylan Browne McMonagle slots at the first bend — if he gets the position just behind Ask Me Again, he controls his own destiny in the straight.

Goddess Of War is an unknown quantity with no public form; if this horse possesses a forward-going style and contests the early lead, it transforms the pace entirely and benefits the hold-up horses at the back.

Spicy Margarita and Hollys Graces are both natural hold-up horses who will struggle to find their preferred position in this congested rear group — watch whether either rider elects to push forward early rather than accept a compromised berth.

Leopold The First's four consecutive runner-up finishes signal a horse that performs consistently but may lack the killer blow — watch whether it can produce a different gear at the business end if it tracks Ask Me Again throughout.
